results.title: A Pragmatic CDO's Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 5
results.content: # **A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 5 — AI That Helps, Not Hypes: ML/GenAI/Agentic Approaches to Data Quality**. ## Where AI earns its keep. We cover label QA and confident learning (Cleanlab), drift detection and robustness (WILDS), feature parity checks, and semantic anomaly detection when rules fail. Agentic runbooks automate lineage walks, owner paging, and contract test generation — always with a human in the loop to keep the system honest. > **Confident Learning for Labels:** Applying confident learning (Cleanlab) to flag label errors and resolve annotator disagreements can significantly boost model performance by cleaning noisy training data [1]. Gold-label audits and active learning loops raise label accuracy, with consensus measured by inter-annotator agreement (e.g. Cohen’s k) [2], [3]. ## Written by Adnan Masood, PhD. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.

results.title: Analyzing Dataset Annotation Quality Management in the ...
results.content: Jan-Christoph Klie, Richard Eckart de Castilho, Iryna Gurevych; Analyzing Dataset Annotation Quality Management in the Wild. While practices and guidelines regarding dataset creation projects exist, to our knowledge, large-scale analysis has yet to be performed on how quality management is conducted when creating natural language datasets and whether these recommendations are followed. Having large, high-quality annotated datasets available is essential for developing, training, evaluating, and deploying reliable machine learning models (Sun et al. Quality management encompasses, among others, proper data selection, choice of annotators and training, creating and improving annotation schemes and guidelines, as well as annotator agreement, data validation, and error rate estimation (Hovy and Lavid 2010; Alex et al. Based on *Papers With Code*,2 we then collect and annotate a large set of publications (591, of which 314 report human annotation or validation) that introduce new text datasets, and analyze how often and how well the different quality management methods are used.
